Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

mind noun

intellect, thoughts

also what’s on your mind?, in my mind, come to mind, out of one’s mind, it had not entered my mind, it never occurred to me, that had never occurred to me, occur to, cross one’s mind, enter one’s mind

classical

Ter. Eun. 816: Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.
Cic. Sen. 38: corpore senex esse poterit, animō numquam erit
Traupman 104: quid tibi in animō est?

animus, animī m.

noun, second declension

mind, heart, spirit

The mind as the seat of thought and feeling: in animō habēre, to have in mind, intend (see mean, intend); ex animō, from the heart; animum advertere, to notice.

Other words

  • mēns, mentis f. — mind, intellect, reason

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.105: hominis autem mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō; Plaut. Amph. 293: Mī in mentem vēnit

    The thinking mind: in mentem venīre, to come into one’s head; mente captus, out of one’s mind (Cic. Ac. 2.53, Lewis & Short).

  • in mentem venīre — come to mind, occur to (someone)

    phrase: what occurs is the subject, the person in the dative · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 2.2.34: quid tibi istuc in mentem venit? (Lewis & Short s.v. mēns); Plaut. Aul. 2.2.49: venit hoc mihi in mentem (Lewis & Short); Traupman 104: it had not entered my mind, mihi in mentem nōn vēnerat; Traupman 105: that had never occurred to me, mihi istuc numquam in mentem vēnerat

    English says “I thought of it”; Latin says “it came into my mind”: mihi in mentem vēnit. With a genitive it means “to remember”: venit mihi Platōnis in mentem is Cicero’s idiom (see remember).

Examples

  • Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.

    My mind has been on the dishes for ages.Ter. Eun. 816

  • hominis autem mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō

    but the human mind is fed by learning and thinkingCic. Off. 1.105

  • quod quī sequitur, corpore senex esse poterit, animō numquam erit

    whoever follows this may be old in body, but will never be old in mindCic. Sen. 38

  • Mihi istuc numquam in mentem vēnerat.

    That had never occurred to me.Traupman 105

See also think, sense, never mind, mean.
